clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia from biallelic variants in GBA2, which encodes the non-lysosomal (cytosol-facing) glucosylceramidase that hydrolyses glucosylceramide to ceramide and glucose.
The distinctive phenotype combines spastic paraplegia with cerebellar ataxia, cataract and cognitive impairment.
Male hypogonadism with testicular hypotrophy and impaired fertility is characteristic, reflecting the enzyme's role in normal sperm development.
Brain MRI typically shows a thin corpus callosum together with cerebellar atrophy.
Onset is usually in infancy or childhood with delayed motor milestones progressing to a spastic gait, often with dysarthria and pes cavus.
GBA2 is allelic with autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxia, so some individuals present with an ataxia-predominant rather than paraplegia-predominant picture.
GBA2 must not be confused with GBA1: GBA1 encodes the lysosomal enzyme deficient in Gaucher disease, whereas GBA2 is a distinct non-lysosomal glucosylceramidase.
The cluster of cataract, cerebellar signs and gonadal dysfunction is a valuable syndromic clue in a young person with spastic paraparesis.
reference.pathophysiology: GBA2 encodes non-lysosomal glucosylceramidase (beta-glucosidase 2), a membrane-associated enzyme acting at the cytosolic face of the endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi that hydrolyses glucosylceramide and thereby helps regulate cellular glycosphingolipid and ceramide balance. Biallelic loss-of-function variants disturb glucosylceramide turnover and the downstream sphingolipid signalling that is critical for myelin, neuronal membrane integrity, lens transparency and spermatogenesis. The resulting combined corticospinal, cerebellar, lenticular and gonadal dysfunction places SPG46 among the sphingolipid and lipid-metabolism complicated spastic paraplegias.
additionalDifferentials: SPG26 (B4GALNT1) — a ganglioside-synthesis defect with cognitive impairment, cerebellar signs and gonadal dysfunction, a very close mimic
SPG5 (CYP7B1) — an oxysterol-metabolism complicated spastic paraplegia
SPG35 (FA2H), SPG54 (DDHD2) and SPG56 (CYP2U1) — other lipid-metabolism complicated forms
Marinesco-Sjogren syndrome — cataract, cerebellar ataxia, hypogonadism and myopathy
Autosomal recessive cerebellar ataxias, including the ataxia-predominant GBA2 phenotype
Gaucher disease (GBA1), which must be distinguished as a separate lysosomal enzyme defect
additionalInvestigations: Gene panel or exome sequencing to identify biallelic GBA2 variants with segregation studies
Brain MRI assessing corpus callosum thickness and cerebellar volume
Endocrine and gonadal assessment in affected males, including testicular examination, hormonal profile and semen analysis interpreted qualitatively
Nerve conduction studies if a peripheral neuropathy is suspected
redFlags: Progressive visual impairment from cataract requiring surgical review
Marked cerebellar decompensation affecting speech and swallowing
reference.prognosis: The disorder is slowly progressive and many affected individuals retain walking into adulthood, often with aids, although combined cerebellar, visual and cognitive involvement adds disability. Fertility is frequently impaired in affected males.
pitfalls: Confusing GBA2 disease with GBA1-related Gaucher disease because of the similar gene name
Overlooking cataract or gonadal features and thereby missing the syndromic clue
Labelling the presentation as a primary cerebellar ataxia when the paraplegia is mild
Missing recessive inheritance in non-consanguineous families
references: Hereditary spastic paraplegia clinical and genetic reviews
management: Symptomatic antispasticity therapy with baclofen or tizanidine, and botulinum toxin for focal spasticity
Physiotherapy with balance and gait training for combined spasticity and cerebellar ataxia, plus orthoses and walking aids
Ophthalmological referral for cataract, including surgical extraction where vision is impaired
Endocrine and fertility assessment in affected males for hypogonadism and impaired spermatogenesis, with hormone replacement and fertility counselling
Neuropsychological support for cognitive impairment and speech therapy for dysarthria
Genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance with carrier testing of relatives
Multidisciplinary neurology, ophthalmology, endocrinology and rehabilitation input
